breathing_note.title: A gentle guide, not a rigid timer
breathing_note.text: The times shown are gentle pacing guides, not strict targets. Let each breath vary naturally within a comfortable range. The rhythm may ebb and flow rather than follow exact seconds.

name: Box Breathing
desc: A simple paced-breathing technique built around four equal phases: inhale, hold, exhale, and hold. The steady rhythm can help settle attention and encourage calm, controlled breathing.
howto: Inhale through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 4, exhale for 4, then hold for 4. Keep every side of the square equal.

name: 4-7-8 Breathing
desc: A slow breathing pattern with a longer exhale. Popularized by Dr. Andrew Weil and inspired by yogic pranayama; it is often used for relaxation and before sleep.
howto: Inhale through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 7, then exhale through the mouth for 8. Repeat for four cycles.

name: Alternate Nostril Breathing
desc: Nadi Shodhana ('channel cleansing') alternates the breath between nostrils. Since airflow through each nostril correlates with the nervous system, this practice helps balance sympathetic and [parasympathetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasympathetic_nervous_system) activity. Note: This practice is for general wellness and is not a substitute for medical treatment.
howto: Close the right nostril and inhale through the left. Close the left and exhale through the right. Inhale through the right, close it, and exhale through the left. Follow the on-screen pulse for each phase.

related.name: Nasal cycle
related.blurb: The natural rhythm controlled by the autonomic nervous system, alternating airflow between nostrils.

name: Long Exhale Breathing
desc: A simple relaxation pattern where exhaling longer than inhaling activates the [parasympathetic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasympathetic_nervous_system), helping to reduce stress. Note: This practice is for general wellness and is not a substitute for medical treatment.
howto: Inhale gently through the nose, then slowly exhale so that the duration of the exhale is about twice as long as the inhale. Maintain a comfortable, unforced rhythm.

name: Bee Breathing
desc: Bhramari, named after the humming sound of a bee. A steady humming sound is produced during the exhale and can feel calming and soothing.
howto: Inhale gently through the nose. Exhale with a low, steady 'hmmm' while keeping the mouth closed. You may gently cover the ears with your fingers for a stronger sense of resonance.

name: Bellows Breathing
desc: Bhastrika (Bellows Breath) is a traditional pranayama characterized by active, rhythmic inhalations and exhalations. It is a stimulating practice rather than a gentle relaxation breath.
howto: Sit upright with relaxed shoulders. Inhale and exhale actively through the nose at a steady 1-to-1 rhythm, allowing the abdomen to move with the breath. Begin with a short set and stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable. People with cardiovascular or blood-pressure conditions should seek appropriate guidance before practicing forceful breathing.

cues.inhale: Breathe in sharply and forcefully through the nose.
cues.exhale: Breathe out sharply and forcefully through the nose.

related.name: Tummo
related.blurb: A Tibetan Buddhist 'inner-fire' practice that also uses vigorous, controlled breathing to generate heat and focus.

related.name: Wim Hof Method
related.blurb: A modern method combining forceful cyclical breathing, cold exposure, and mindset training, in the same lineage of vigorous breathwork.

name: Belly Breathing
desc: A gentle breathing practice associated with dantian-focused traditions of qigong. Attention is placed on the lower abdomen while the breath remains slow and comfortable.
howto: Rest one hand on the lower abdomen. Inhale gently and allow the abdomen to expand. Exhale slowly and allow it to soften. Keep the breath comfortable rather than forcing the movement.

name: Eye & Mind Soothing Breath
desc: A soothing practice that combines soft breathing with gentle relaxation around the eyes. Easing tension around the eyes directly signals the [trigeminal nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigeminal_nerve) to help shift the body into a rest-and-digest state. Note: This practice is for general wellness and is not a substitute for medical treatment.
howto: Close your eyes softly and inhale gently. As you exhale, imagine releasing all tightness around your eyelids, forehead, and temples. Keep your face completely relaxed without applying physical pressure.

name: Neck & Throat Release Breath
desc: A gentle exercise connecting breath with neck and throat awareness. Releasing tension around the throat and vocal area helps stimulate the [vagus nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagus_nerve), encouraging deep relaxation. Note: This practice is for general wellness and is not a substitute for medical treatment.
howto: Inhale gently, letting your neck and shoulders stay soft and relaxed. Hold softly, then exhale deeply while releasing any tightness in your jaw and throat. Focus on a comfortable, easy breath without forcing the posture.
